name: A Tribe Called Quest
hook: A Queens group that built rap on jazz records and low end, and whose leader brought J Dilla into the wider world.
blurb: Q-Tip, Phife Dawg, Ali Shaheed Muhammad and Jarobi White came from St. Albans, Queens. They were part of the Native Tongues, a group of friendly, thoughtful rap acts. Their second album, The Low End Theory, in 1991, was built on jazz records and deep bass, and the jazz bassist Ron Carter played on it. Their importance runs on two tracks. Their records made the jazz sample a mainstream sound in rap. And Q-Tip's production team, The Ummah, was the route by which J Dilla's work reached the whole country. Q-Tip, who learned sampling partly from Large Professor, met a young Detroit producer, Jay Dee, in 1994, introduced by the Detroit musician Amp Fiddler, and brought him into The Ummah with himself and Ali Shaheed Muhammad. Phife Dawg died in March 2016, and the group's last album, We Got It from Here... Thank You 4 Your Service, came out eight months later, in November.
